blocks.text: A sacred healing secret of the Himalayas.

The mountains spend centuries pressing ancient plant matter between layers of rock until it becomes a dense mineral essence. It only appears above 16,000 feet, in summer, when the sun warms the cliffs and it seeps out. People have climbed up and gathered it by hand for thousands of years, and Ayurvedic practice has used it that whole time. The old Sanskrit name translates to destroyer of weakness.
What makes it rare is what it carries: 85+ trace minerals in ionic form, the charged form your cells absorb directly, plus a compound called fulvic acid that helps your cells turn fuel into energy.
Raw, it is bitter and hard to take. We fold it into a caramel honey stick instead.

panels.title: Why a frequency company sells honey

blocks.text: Because your brainwaves are made of minerals.

Every frequency you feel in the headphones is your neurons firing, and neurons fire by moving charged mineral ions across a membrane. That is what an action potential physically is. Each firing also costs energy your mitochondria have to produce on the spot.
So the headphones tune the signal. The minerals are what your brain makes the signal out of. Modern food, grown in tired soil, barely delivers them anymore.
Tune the signal. Feed the signal. That is the whole practice.
This is a compounding mineral, never a stimulant. Nothing spikes on day one. Here is the arc people consistently report.
